question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=4x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $\pi /12$ | $\pi /8$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\pi /3$ | $\pi /2$ |

Using the above, we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /12}^{\pi /8}3{csc}^{2}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}3{csc}^{2}⁡(u)\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}{csc}^{2}⁡(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(-\operatorname{cot}⁡(u))\,{|}_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(0+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
